title: Claw reversal after amputation depends on regeneration versus growth rates

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Claw reversal after amputation depends on regeneration versus growth rates

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Whether an amputated large crustacean claw regenerates as the large claw, or the claws exchange roles, depends on the ratio between the regenerative growth rate of the amputated claw and the growth rate of the uninjured claw, since claw form follows claw size.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It depends upon the respective rates of growth, upon a ratio between the rate of regeneration and the rate of growth of the uninjured limb

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Regeneration”. Scope: Crustacea with asymmetric claws (lobster, Alpheus, crabs)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-32: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed rate ratio and fate outcome make a clear prospective test. Public literature documents claw regeneration, but the paired longitudinal variables needed to adjudicate this mechanism appear insufficient.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For individually tracked asymmetric-clawed crustaceans, estimate post-amputation growth rates of both claws and test whether their ratio predicts retention versus reversal of claw identity and morphology. A threshold relationship that predicts outcomes independently of species and body size would support the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Neural and positional effects could confound a rate-only explanation.

The required individual-level bilateral growth trajectories are rarely archived.

data existence: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decision variable is a ratio of two growth rates, which experiments have sometimes recorded. There is no compiled public series, and the taxonomic scope is several heterochelous groups studied separately. Even a compiled table would leave neural and molt-stage programs as serious alternative causes of the same reversal.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After claw amputation, measure the regenerative growth rate of the stump and the growth rate of the intact claw, and predict reversal from whether the intact claw reaches the large-claw size class first. Reversal when and only when that ratio favours the intact claw would support the claim; reversal uncorrelated with the two rates would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Form-follows-size has to be granted before the rate ratio is interpreted.

Paired rate measurements are spread across lobster, snapping-shrimp and crab papers.

Nerve supply, molt stage and a handedness program can reverse claws at the same sizes.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.55
